sentences.text: Purpose.
sentences.say: Purpose.

sentences.text: A model is only as good as the evidence that it works.
sentences.say: A model is only as good as the evidence that it works.

sentences.text: This chapter is about gathering that evidence honestly: which numbers to compute, on which data, and how to avoid fooling yourself.
sentences.say: This chapter is about gathering that evidence honestly: which numbers to compute, on which data, and how to avoid fooling yourself.

sentences.text: It is the same skill you will need to evaluate an LLM system.
sentences.say: It is the same skill you will need to evaluate an LLM system.

sentences.text: This chapter is almost entirely beyond the videos.
sentences.say: This chapter is almost entirely beyond the videos.

sentences.text: It comes from standard practice and the scikit-learn documentation.
sentences.say: It comes from standard practice and the scikit-learn documentation.

sentences.text: Key ideas
sentences.say: Key ideas

sentences.text: Accuracy can look great while the model is useless, whenever one class is rare.
sentences.say: Accuracy can look great while the model is useless, whenever one class is rare.

sentences.text: The confusion matrix counts the four kinds of outcome.
sentences.say: The confusion matrix counts the four kinds of outcome.

sentences.text: Precision and recall each summarize one kind of error.
sentences.say: Precision and recall each summarize one kind of error.

sentences.text: A threshold trades precision for recall.
sentences.say: A threshold trades precision for recall.

sentences.text: Choose it with the real cost of each mistake.
sentences.say: Choose it with the real cost of each mistake.

sentences.text: Evaluate on data the model has not seen, with cross-validation for small datasets and date-based splits for time-ordered ones.
sentences.say: Evaluate on data the model has not seen, with cross-validation for small datasets and date-based splits for time-ordered ones.

sentences.text: A predicted probability should match reality (calibration) when decisions depend on it.
sentences.say: A predicted probability should match reality (calibration) when decisions depend on it.

sentences.text: 12.1 Why accuracy lies
sentences.say: 12.1 Why accuracy lies

sentences.text: Take 1,000 loans, of which 50 defaulted.
sentences.say: Take 1,000 loans, of which 50 defaulted.

sentences.text: A "model" that predicts "no default" for everyone is 95% accurate and catches no defaulter at all.
sentences.say: A "model" that predicts "no default" for everyone is 95 percent accurate and catches no defaulter at all.

sentences.text: Accuracy hides the thing you care about, because defaults are rare.
sentences.say: Accuracy hides the thing you care about, because defaults are rare.

sentences.text: Whenever classes are imbalanced (fraud, defaults, rare diseases), look at the next measures instead.
sentences.say: Whenever classes are imbalanced (fraud, defaults, rare diseases), look at the next measures instead.

sentences.text: 12.2 The confusion matrix
sentences.say: 12.2 The confusion matrix

sentences.text: Suppose a model flags 60 loans as risky.
sentences.say: Suppose a model flags 60 loans as risky.

sentences.text: Of its 60 flags, 35 really were defaults and 25 were good loans flagged by mistake.
sentences.say: Of its 60 flags, 35 really were defaults and 25 were good loans flagged by mistake.

sentences.text: It missed 15 defaults.
sentences.say: It missed 15 defaults.

sentences.text: Everything else, 925 loans, was correctly left alone.
sentences.say: Everything else, 925 loans, was correctly left alone.

sentences.text: The "always no default" model: accuracy 0.95, recall 0.0.
sentences.say: The "always no default" model: accuracy 0.95, recall 0.0.

sentences.text: Exactly the failure accuracy hides.
sentences.say: Exactly the failure accuracy hides.

sentences.text: Which mistake costs more?
sentences.say: Which mistake costs more?

sentences.text: Suppose a missed default costs 5,000 euros and a wrongly flagged good loan costs 200 euros of lost margin (invented numbers).
sentences.say: Suppose a missed default costs 5,000 euros and a wrongly flagged good loan costs 200 euros of lost margin (invented numbers).

sentences.text: The model above costs 15 x 5,000 + 25 x 200 = 80,000 euros.
sentences.say: The model above costs 15 times 5,000 plus 25 times 200 equals 80,000 euros.

sentences.text: Approving everyone costs 50 x 5,000 = 250,000 euros.
sentences.say: Approving everyone costs 50 times 5,000 equals 250,000 euros.

sentences.text: The business question is never "is accuracy high" but "which mix of errors is cheapest".
sentences.say: The business question is never "is accuracy high" but "which mix of errors is cheapest".

sentences.text: 12.3 Thresholds
sentences.say: 12.3 Thresholds

sentences.text: A classifier gives a probability, and the threshold turns it into a yes or no (Chapter 9).
sentences.say: A classifier gives a probability, and the threshold turns it into a yes or no (Chapter 9).

sentences.text: Moving it changes both numbers.
sentences.say: Moving it changes both numbers.

sentences.text: On a held-out set of 80 cases (20% of the Chapter 10 data, scored by scikit-learn's default logistic regression):
sentences.say: On a held-out set of 80 cases (20 percent of the Chapter 10 data, scored by scikit-learn's default logistic regression):

sentences.text: A lower threshold flags more cases: it catches more of the real positives (higher recall) and makes more false alarms (lower precision).
sentences.say: A lower threshold flags more cases: it catches more of the real positives (higher recall) and makes more false alarms (lower precision).

sentences.text: A higher threshold is stricter, with the reverse effect.
sentences.say: A higher threshold is stricter, with the reverse effect.

sentences.text: Pick the threshold where the total cost is lowest.
sentences.say: Pick the threshold where the total cost is lowest.

sentences.text: The ROC curve plots recall against the false alarm rate for every possible threshold, and its area (AUC) summarizes a model's ranking ability in one number: 0.5 is random, 1.0 is perfect.
sentences.say: The ROC curve plots recall against the false alarm rate for every possible threshold, and its area (AUC) summarizes a model's ranking ability in one number: 0.5 is random, 1.0 is perfect.

sentences.text: This model's AUC is 0.915.
sentences.say: This model's AUC is 0.915.

sentences.text: For rare classes, a precision-recall curve is more informative than ROC.
sentences.say: For rare classes, a precision-recall curve is more informative than ROC.

sentences.text: 12.4 Metrics for regression
sentences.say: 12.4 Metrics for regression

sentences.text: For numbers: MAE, RMSE and R squared (Chapter 5).
sentences.say: For numbers: MAE, RMSE and R squared (Chapter 5).

sentences.text: Report the error in the original units, for example "typically 22 euros off", and compare it with the baseline of always predicting the average.
sentences.say: Report the error in the original units, for example "typically 22 euros off", and compare it with the baseline of always predicting the average.

sentences.text: 12.5 Evaluating without fooling yourself
sentences.say: 12.5 Evaluating without fooling yourself

sentences.text: Hold-out.
sentences.say: Hold-out.

sentences.text: Fit on the training set, score on a test set the model never touched.
sentences.say: Fit on the training set, score on a test set the model never touched.

sentences.text: Use the test set once.
sentences.say: Use the test set once.

sentences.text: Cross-validation.
sentences.say: Cross-validation.

sentences.text: With little data, split into k parts (often 5), train on k - 1 parts, score on the remaining one, rotate, and average.
sentences.say: With little data, split into k parts (often 5), train on k minus 1 parts, score on the remaining one, rotate, and average.

sentences.text: It uses every row for testing exactly once and shows how much the score varies.
sentences.say: It uses every row for testing exactly once and shows how much the score varies.

sentences.text: Time-based splits.
sentences.say: Time-based splits.

sentences.text: For loans and anything with dates, train on the past and test on the future.
sentences.say: For loans and anything with dates, train on the past and test on the future.

sentences.text: A random split lets the model learn from rows that are "after" the ones it is tested on.
sentences.say: A random split lets the model learn from rows that are "after" the ones it is tested on.

sentences.text: Leakage.
sentences.say: Leakage.

sentences.text: Any feature that would not exist at decision time ruins all of the above (Chapter 3).
sentences.say: Any feature that would not exist at decision time ruins all of the above (Chapter 3).

sentences.text: Five scores between 0.838 and 0.888: the spread is itself information.
sentences.say: Five scores between 0.838 and 0.888: the spread is itself information.

sentences.text: A difference between two models smaller than that spread is probably noise.
sentences.say: A difference between two models smaller than that spread is probably noise.

sentences.text: 12.6 Calibration
sentences.say: 12.6 Calibration

sentences.text: When a model says 0.7, do about 70% of such cases turn out positive?
sentences.say: When a model says 0.7, do about 70 percent of such cases turn out positive?

sentences.text: If yes, it is calibrated.
sentences.say: If yes, it is calibrated.

sentences.text: Calibration matters when you use the probability itself, for pricing, provisioning or ranking by risk, rather than only the yes or no. A reliability diagram groups predictions into bins (0 to 0.1, 0.1 to 0.2, and so on) and plots the predicted probability against the observed share of positives; a calibrated model lies on the diagonal.
sentences.say: Calibration matters when you use the probability itself, for pricing, provisioning or ranking by risk, rather than only the yes or no. A reliability diagram groups predictions into bins (0 to 0.1, 0.1 to 0.2, and so on) and plots the predicted probability against the observed share of positives; a calibrated model lies on the diagonal.

sentences.text: The Brier score (the average squared gap between probability and outcome, lower is better) measures it in one number: 0.118 for the held-out set above.
sentences.say: The Brier score (the average squared gap between probability and outcome, lower is better) measures it in one number: 0.118 for the held-out set above.

sentences.text: Logistic regression is often well calibrated by default.
sentences.say: Logistic regression is often well calibrated by default.

sentences.text: Tree ensembles and neural networks often are not, and can be corrected with scikit-learn's calibration tools.
sentences.say: Tree ensembles and neural networks often are not, and can be corrected with scikit-learn's calibration tools.

sentences.text: This is the idea behind the calibration page planned for your stock platform.
sentences.say: This is the idea behind the calibration page planned for your stock platform.

sentences.text: 12.7 The same ideas evaluate LLM systems
sentences.say: 12.7 The same ideas evaluate LLM systems

sentences.text: Everything here carries over.
sentences.say: Everything here carries over.

sentences.text: A gold set of questions with known answers plays the role of labelled data.
sentences.say: A gold set of questions with known answers plays the role of labelled data.

sentences.text: For text-to-SQL, the score is execution accuracy: does the generated query return the same rows as your gold query?
sentences.say: For text-to-SQL, the score is execution accuracy: does the generated query return the same rows as your gold query?

sentences.text: For retrieval (Chapter 18), it is hit@k: is the right passage among the top k?
sentences.say: For retrieval (Chapter 18), it is hit@k: is the right passage among the top k?

sentences.text: An "LLM as judge" that grades answers is a classifier, so you check it against human labels with a confusion matrix, exactly as above.
sentences.say: An "LLM as judge" that grades answers is a classifier, so you check it against human labels with a confusion matrix, exactly as above.

sentences.text: And you always compare with a baseline.
sentences.say: And you always compare with a baseline.
